title: Flatification of a projective generic curve and its horizontal marking
statement: Let $S$ be an excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring] integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] scheme with generic point [def-sc-generic-point] $\eta$. Let $h:C\to S$ be projective in the finite-projective-space sense [def-kun-projective], with $C$ integral and $C_\eta$ a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] irreducible curve of dimension $1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $H\subset C$ be the schematic closure of a finite etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] closed subscheme $H_\eta\subset C_\eta$ (possibly empty). There is an excellent integral Noetherian scheme $S_1$ and a projective-bundle birational morphism $v:S_1\to S$, which is a blowup with centre disjoint from a dense open of $S$, with the following properties. The schematic closures $C_1$ and $H_1$ of $C_\eta\times_S S_1$ and $H_\eta\times_S S_1$ in $C\times_S S_1$ are the strict transforms. The scheme $C_1$ is integral, $H_1\subset C_1$ is closed, $C_1\to S_1$ is projective in the finite-projective-space sense, flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] with every geometric fibre of pure dimension $1$, and $H_1\to S_1$ is finite, flat and finitely presented with all nonempty geometric fibres of pure dimension $0$. These transforms have their original generic fibres, and the projection $C_1\to C$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and birational. A blowup in an ideal sheaf $I$ is the relative Proj of $\bigoplus_{n\geq0}I^n$; schematic closure is defined by the kernel of restriction of functions to the given subscheme.

source.place: Exposé X, proof of Theorem 3.4, Step 2, printed p. 160 (flatten simultaneously the curve and the horizontal boundary). proof.text: By [lem-pc-projective-proper], $C\to S$ is proper. The closed immersion $H\hookrightarrow C$ is proper and proper maps compose by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], so $H\to S$ is proper too. Thus $C\amalg H\to S$ is of finite type and separated, hence quasi-separated. Apply [lem-sbc-generic-flat-finite-presentation] to this finite disjoint union over the integral base $S$. It gives a nonempty open $U\subset S$ over which both $C$ and $H$ are flat and locally finitely presented. Since $S$ is Noetherian, $U$ is quasi-compact. The empty marking causes no change to this argument.

source.place: Tags 01W9 and 052A; choose a common generic-flat open before ILO X Theorem 3.4 Step 2.

proof.text: Apply the flattening theorem [lem-trf-flattening-by-admissible-blowup] to $W=C\amalg H$ and $T=S$, with $U$ from Step 1: $S$ is Noetherian, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated, $U$ is quasi-compact, and $W\to S$ is of finite type and quasi-separated by Step 1. By [def-nagata-admissible-blowup] we obtain a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $I$, with $I|_U=\mathcal O_U$, and $v:S_1=\operatorname{Bl}_I S\to S$. Denote the two strict transforms by $\widetilde C$ and $\widetilde H$. Schematic closure is computed by a kernel of restriction, and on a disjoint union that kernel is computed componentwise. Thus the transformed disjoint union is $\widetilde C\amalg\widetilde H$, so each component is flat and finitely presented over $S_1$. By [lemma-nagata-strict-transform-closure-characterization], these are the schematic closures of the restrictions over the complement of the centre.

source.place: Tag 081R, lemma-flat-after-blowing-up, applied once to C disjoint union H; strict-transform closure: Divisors Tag 080D, definition-strict-transform.

proof.text: Locally on $S$, write $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $I=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)$. The degree-one standard charts of $\operatorname{Proj}(\bigoplus I^n)$ have rings $A[I/a_i]$; this is the degree-zero part after inverting $a_i$ in degree one. Charts with $a_i=0$ are empty, and for $a_i\ne0$ their rings are subrings of $\operatorname{Frac}A$. They are domains. Over the complement of $V(I)$ the ideal is the unit ideal, and $\operatorname{Proj}\mathcal O[t]=S$ there. Each nonempty chart contains this same generic point; hence $S_1$ is integral and $v$ is an isomorphism over a dense open containing $U$, so is birational. The finite-type ideal gives properness of $v$ by [lemma-nagata-blowup-proper], hence finite type. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $S_1$ Noetherian, and [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent], applied on affine base charts and localizations, makes it excellent.

source.place: Tag 0804, lemma-blowing-up-affine (standard-chart computation); finite-type ideals and properness; More on Algebra Tag 07QU.

proof.text: The multiplication map $\operatorname{Sym} I\twoheadrightarrow\bigoplus_{n\geq0}I^n$ is surjective in each degree: the degree-$n$ part is generated by products of $n$ local sections of $I$. The surjective-graded-map clause of [prop-nagata-relative-proj-functoriality] gives $S_1\hookrightarrow\mathbf P_S(I)$. Since $I$ is quasi-coherent of finite type, this is exactly projective-bundle projectivity by [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism]. For the curve, [lem-pc-projective-base-change] embeds $C\times_S S_1$ in $\mathbf P^N_{S_1}$. Composing its embedding with the closed embedding of $\widetilde C$ exhibits $\widetilde C\to S_1$ as H-projective: the composite of closed embeddings is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e).

source.place: Tag 02NS, lemma-blowing-up-projective, first assertion and its displayed Sym-to-Rees surjection; projective base change Tag 01WF.

proof.text: The strict transforms agree with $C$ and $H$ over $U$; their generic fibres are therefore the specified $C_\eta$ and $H_\eta$. Here $\kappa(\eta_1)=\kappa(\eta)$ because $v$ is an isomorphism near the generic point. To identify the transforms with closures of these generic fibres, at a point of either transform put $A=\mathcal O_{S_1,s}$ and $B=\mathcal O_{\widetilde X,x}$. By [def-weil-flat-morphism] $B$ is flat over the domain $A$. The defining injectivity criterion [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], applied to $A\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Frac}A$, injects $B$ into $B\otimes_A\operatorname{Frac}A$. Thus no nonzero local function vanishes after restriction to the generic fibre. That fibre is schematically dense in the transform, and is topologically dense as well: this nonzero localization has a prime giving a generalization over the generic point. Since each transform is closed in the ambient base change, it is precisely the schematic closure of its generic fibre. Consequently $\widetilde C=C_1$ and $\widetilde H=H_1$ as defined in the statement.

source.place: Tag 081R and strict-transform closure; the generic-density identification is the displayed flat localization injection.

proof.text: For $X=C_1$, the localized rings in Step 5 are localizations of affine rings of the integral generic curve $C_\eta$, hence domains. Their subrings $B$ are domains too, so $C_1$ is reduced. The dense irreducible generic fibre makes $C_1$ irreducible, hence integral. The generic closed inclusion $H_\eta\subset C_\eta$ implies that its schematic closure $H_1$ is contained as a closed subscheme in the schematic closure $C_1$: the restriction kernel for $C_\eta$ is contained in that for $H_\eta$. The map $C\times_S S_1\to C$ is proper by base change of proper $v$, and $C_1$ is closed in it. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](a)--(c), $C_1\to C$ is proper. It is an isomorphism over the dense open $C_U$ of the integral $C$, so is birational.

source.place: Strict transforms and proper base change, with the schematic-closure kernel construction; ILO X Theorem 3.4 Step 2.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-flat-dense-generic-fibre-pure-dimension] to $C_1\to S_1$ with $d=1$. Flatness and finite presentation come from Step 2, generic density from Step 5, and its generic fibre is the original irreducible dimension-one curve. Thus every nonempty geometric fibre is pure of dimension $1$. These fibres are all nonempty: [lem-pc-projective-proper] makes $C_1\to S_1$ proper, so its image is closed and contains the generic point, and is therefore all of $S_1$. Apply the same dimension lemma to $H_1\to S_1$ with $d=0$. Its generic fibre is finite etale; [lem-weil-pbc-etale-smooth-zero-dimensional-fibres] gives dimension zero at every point, so each generic irreducible component has dimension zero. Step 5 again gives density. Every nonempty geometric fibre of $H_1$ is therefore pure of dimension $0$. If $H_\eta$ is empty its schematic closure $H_1$ is empty, and the dimension assertions are vacuous.

source.place: Tags 0GSJ--0GSK with F=O; Morphisms Tag 02NK for geometric fibres; dimensions d=1 and d=0.

proof.text: Because $H_1$ is closed in the proper $S_1$-scheme $C_1$, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](a),(c) makes $H_1\to S_1$ proper. Its fibres have dimension zero by Step 7. On any affine pair, [lem-weil-pbc-ring-quasifinite-zero-fibre-dimension] therefore makes the ring map quasi-finite at every fibre prime. This is local quasi-finiteness in [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Now [pqf-lem-proper-lqf-finite] gives finiteness. Flatness and finite presentation already hold by Step 2. Together with Steps 3--7, this gives every requested property of the single blowup and both strict transforms.

lean.note: Uses the canonical admissible blowup and strict-transform APIs. Closed immersions and equality of their kernel ideal sheaves specify the closures and strict transforms up to their unique isomorphisms over the ambient schemes. Generic-fibre pullback squares include their embedding compatibility. Finite presentation is locally finite presentation together with the quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness supplied by H-projectivity or finiteness.
